newsitem.title: USA: Simpson civil trial jury is mix of races and ages.
newsitem.headline: Simpson civil trial jury is mix of races and ages.

text.p: The following is a breakdown of the jury chosen Thursday in the O.J. Simpson civil trial. The panellists' names have been kept confidential and they are known only by their juror numbers:
-- Juror #199: a man who was born in Jamaica, is of mixed Asian and black descent and appears to be in his 20s. He is a postal worker with a degree from the California State University in Fresno.
-- Juror #341: a white woman who appears to be about 70 years old. She wrote on her jury questionnaire that, in her opinion, the use of force in a relationship often predisposes a person to violence.

-- Juror #427: a white man who appears to be in his 30s. The man, who is studying to be a firefighter, wrote on his questionnaire that he is concerned about Simpson's two young children from his marriage to murder victim Nicole Brown Simpson.

-- Juror #78: a woman of mixed white and Hispanic descent who appears to be in her 20s. She said during the questioning of prospective jurors that she didn't believe celebrities are given special treatment by police officers.

-- Juror #266: a white woman who appears to be in her 30s. The woman, who grew up in the South, believes that interracial couples have a harder time than most other marriages. She works as a stage manager for a community theatre.

-- Juror #257: a Hispanic woman who appears to be in her 30s. She indicated on her jury questionnaire that she didn't pay much attention to Simpson's criminal trial -- in which he was acquitted of double murder -- and had few opinions about the case.

-- Juror #333: a black woman who appears to be in her 60s. She told attorneys she felt sympathy for Fred Goldman, the father of murder victim Ronald Goldman, because "it's a parent's worst nightmare to have your child die before you."
-- Juror #290, a man in his 40s believed to be of Middle Eastern descent. He told attorneys that he is a good listener who will "go in with an open mind."
-- Juror #8: a black man who appears to be in his 40s. The man, who served in the military for 20 years, has both a brother and a nephew in the FBI and has been in an interracial relationship.

-- Juror #215: a white woman who appears to be in her 60s. The woman, who once met Simpson in a shoe store, wrote on a jury questionnaire that she thought the defendant was "probably not guilty" of the murders.
-- Juror #88: a white woman who appears to be in her 30s.
-- Juror #227: a white man who appears to be in his 50s or 60s. The man, who said his father had been a police officer, called interracial marriages "impractical."
